text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is a city in y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ InState(Billings, Montana) ::: Billings is a city in Montana.
InState(Montana, U.S.) ∧ City(Butte) ∧ City(Helena) ∧ City(Missoula) ::: Montana includes Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
InState(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InState(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in the same state in U.S.
City(StPierre) ∧ ¬InState(StPierre, Montana) ::: The city of St Pierre is not in the state of Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InState(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y ((InCity(x, y) ∧ City(x) ∧ City(y)) → (InState(x, z) ∧ InState(y, z))) ::: A city can only be in one state in U.S.
Conclusion:
InSameState(Butte, StPierre) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in the same state.
